newsitem.title: USA: Dole drops in Reuters poll after Perot bid fails.
newsitem.headline: Dole drops in Reuters poll after Perot bid fails.

text.p: By Alan Elsner, Political Correspondent
Republican Bob Dole lost ground following his abortive overture to Ross Perot and trails President Bill Clinton by 11 percentage points in the Reuters daily tracking poll released on Friday.

Clinton led Dole by 46.2 percent to 35.2 percent in the poll, conducted for Reuters by John Zogby Group International. Reform Party candidate Perot's support stood at six percent and 10.7 percent of respondents remained undecided.

The tracking poll surveys approximately 900 likely voters over a three day period, creating a new three-day rolling average each day. Friday's results involve the average of Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday polling. The margin of sampling error is plus or minus 3.3 percentage points.

Dole had closed the gap with Clinton to 8.7 percent Wednesday but lost support in Thursday's polling after news reports that his campaign manager had flown to Dallas to appeal to Perot to quit the campaign and endorse the Republican nominee. Perot rejected the entreaty.
"A particularly bad day for Bob Dole resulted from the disastrous attempt to push Ross Perot out of the race," said pollster John Zogby.
"Today's results show Dole losing in every region and every age group, and losing ground among moderate voters where Clinton now leads 57.7 percent to 25.7 percent," he said.
Daily tracking polls can produce sharp fluctuations because of the relatively small size of the daily sample. Their main value is in plotting trends over a number of days.

Viewed in this light, the presidential race has been remarkably stable since the poll began Oct 1. In that time, Dole's support has never exceeded 38 percent, while Clinton's has never fallen below 43 percent.

In the past week, both candidates have moved in an extremely narrow range. Dole has been stuck between a high of 36.3 percent and a low of 33.1 percent. Clinton has varied from a high of 46.2 percent and a low of 43.6 percent.

The battle for control of Congress continues to be close with 38.2 percent saying they will vote for the Republican candidate in their congressional district, while 37.3 percent will back the Democrat.
In a hopeful sign for Republicans, three-quarters of Dole supporters said they would vote for their Republican candidate for the House of Representatives.
Less than two-thirds of Clinton supporters plan to back the Democrat in their local congressional district.
